newsitem.title: USA: CSCE July coffee tumbles in spec-led sell-off.
newsitem.headline: CSCE July coffee tumbles in spec-led sell-off.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures plummeted Monday morning, as speculators followed through on Friday's heavy sell-off, traders said.

July arabicas tumbled through key support at 250.00 cents per lb to bottom at 247.50 cents. At 0956 EDT, July stood at 251.00 ents per lb, down 25.40 cents. Second-month September was 21.30 lower, at 217.00, while the back months were 9.00 lower to 2.60 higher.
At the outset, coffee prices gapped down some 6.00 cents, defying the pre-opening call of up 10.00 cents, as traders moved to extend Friday's steep losses.
Some traders said the exchange's move to raise margins may have forced more speculators out of the market.
"I believe a lot of it is related to margins," said one trader. "Also the market was way overdone and there isn't any prospect of a freeze."

After Friday's close, the CSCE said it will raise margins on the July 1997 "C" coffee contract to $12,000 including a $4,000 spot charge, and the September 1997 margin to $10,000, including a $2,000 spot charge, effective today.
The margins on all other contracts were increased by $2,000 to $8,000, the exchange said.

Meanwhile, Weather Services Corp. said Monday no damaging cold is expected this week in Brazil's coffee belt. Temperatures will near to above normal, it said. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk, 212 859 1640))
